provisions.summary: Conditional permanent resident status lasts 10 years unless the Secretary extends it. The Secretary must give notice of the title’s provisions and status-removal requirements when status is granted.
details: The Secretary may revoke status only after determining that the alien no longer meets the requirements referenced in section 102(b)(1)(C), and after giving notice and an opportunity for a hearing.
An alien whose conditional status expires or is revoked returns to the immigration status held immediately before receiving conditional status.

provisions.summary: The Secretary generally must remove conditional status and grant lawful permanent residence when specified eligibility requirements are met. The referenced sections include qualifications whose full meanings are not supplied.
details: The ordinary route requires the alien to meet the referenced section 102(b)(1)(C), not to have abandoned U.S. residence while conditionally resident, and to meet at least one education, service, or earned-income route.
The education route is a higher-education degree, at least two years in good standing in a qualifying postsecondary program, or a recognized postsecondary credential from a qualifying school.
The service route requires at least two years in the Uniformed Services and, if discharged, an honorable discharge.

The income route requires earned income for periods totaling at least three years and at least 75% of the time the alien had valid employment authorization. For specified education enrollment, reduce the three-year total by those enrollment periods.

A hardship route requires the referenced requirements in (a)(1)(A) and (B), compelling circumstances preventing completion of (a)(1)(C), and disability, full-time caregiving, or specified removal hardship.
Unless the disability exception applies, conditional status cannot be removed unless the alien demonstrates satisfaction of the requirements referenced in INA section 312(a).
The Secretary may require a reasonable processing-cost fee for removal applications, subject to the section 303(c) exemption. No dollar amount is stated here.
The Secretary may not remove conditional status until section 302 requirements are satisfied. Applicants may apply for removal at any time after meeting subsection (a)’s eligibility requirements.
For naturalization purposes, conditional residents are treated as admitted and present as lawful permanent residents, but may not apply for naturalization while conditional status continues.

In specified initial applications, the Secretary or Attorney General shall adjust an eligible applicant directly to permanent resident status without conditional status, subject to stated hardship, disability, background-check, and fee provisions.

provisions.summary: Eligible nationals covered by this section must apply within three years after enactment, meet its physical-presence and admissibility requirements, and fit one of two specified protected-status or deferred-enforced-departure categories. The Secretary must charge a processing fee capped at $1,140, subject to exemption.
details: Category one covers specified nationals or stateless people associated with a country designated for TPS on January 1, 2017, who then had or were otherwise eligible for TPS and have not since engaged in conduct that would make them ineligible under the referenced INA provision.
Category two covers people eligible for Deferred Enforced Departure as of January 20, 2021, who have not since engaged in conduct that would make them ineligible for that status.

The applicant must apply, including required section 307 documents, within three years after enactment; have at least three years of continuous physical presence in the United States; and, subject to subsection (c), not be inadmissible under the listed INA grounds.

The Secretary may waive specified inadmissibility grounds for humanitarian purposes, family unity, or the public interest. The waiver authority has an exception for convictions that would otherwise make the alien ineligible under the referenced INA provision.
The Secretary must require a reasonable fee commensurate with processing cost, no more than $1,140, subject to the section 303(c) exemption.

The Secretary may not grant permanent resident status on a conditional basis under this section until section 302 requirements are satisfied. The section describes adjustment to lawful permanent residence; it does not establish that status is conditional.

On request to withdraw, the Secretary must stop processing and close the case. Withdrawal does not prejudice a future application for an immigration benefit under this title or the Immigration and Nationality Act.
